mechanism: Label historical bars long/short via ZigZag (reversal distance 0.0035), shift label one bar ahead as categorical target; train Random Forest (bagging over rows + random predictor subsets at nodes; majority vote across ~100–500 trees) on multi-pair predictors to classify next-bar trend class without accumulating multi-step forecast error.
data_needed: H1 closes of six pairs; ZigZag labels; MAs 5/10/15 diffs, MACD(12,26,9), RSI 14/21/28, quote increments; train/valid/test partition; OOB and confusion-matrix error.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD, GBPUSD, USDCHF, USDJPY, EURGBP, USDCAD H1; 2011-01-10 to 2013-12-24; ~18083 bars
why_new_for_mis: Classification sensor of future trend class (not price regression) with OOB robustness and MeanDecreaseAccuracy/Gini importance for noise-predictor pruning—MIS regime-direction feature from multi-FX cross predictors.
quote: if the trading system is trend-following by design, then the model has to predict trends. The model has to be trained to recognize trends, the target variable has to take only two values "buy" and "sell".

mechanism: Convert bar clock to a 24-level categorical hour factor and calendar date to a 5-level weekday factor; let the classifier discover latent quote dependence on time-of-day and day-of-week without hand-coded session rules.
data_needed: Bar datetime; categorical encoding of hour (24) and weekday (5); joined to price/indicator predictors.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Same six FX pairs H1 as RF study
why_new_for_mis: Session/schedule regime features learned inside the classifier rather than hard-coded Asian/London/NY boxes—MIS can treat hour/weekday levels as soft regime covariates.
quote: In our models, taking into account some hidden data on the quotes dependency on the time of day and day of the week can be revealed by the classification models automatically.

mechanism: Smooth EURUSD Open with Hodrick–Prescott (lambda=10) to separate deterministic HP from residual; fit quotes = C1·HP(-1)+C2·D(HP(-1))+C3·D(HP(-2)); diagnose residual via ACF, normality, GARCH-type and White heteroscedasticity—use residual properties as forward stability sensor of the trading model.
data_needed: EURUSD Open series (~118–236 bars); HP filter; regression fit; residual ACF/normality/White/GARCH tests.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1; sample week 2011-09-12 to 2011-09-17; also rolling windows of 118 and 236 bars
why_new_for_mis: Treats residual heteroscedasticity and lag correlation—not forecast error alone—as the MIS sensor of whether the local price-generating regime is stable enough to trust directional forecasts.
quote: the characteristics of this residual will help us estimate the future stability of the trading system.

mechanism: Fixed-width rolling window re-estimates HP+regression each step; one-step-ahead forecast kotir_f; trend = kotir_f(i+1)-kotir(i); score hit when trend·d(kotir)>0; track profit-factor, consecutive losses, recovery factor as live authenticity of short-horizon direction sensor.
data_needed: Sliding Open window (e.g. 118 bars); EViews/MT4 file exchange of forecast and SE; increment series.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD; EA on M1 with StepForecast=60 (H1 step); 2011-09-12 to 2011-09-16
why_new_for_mis: Operational one-step direction-change sensor with sample-length sensitivity (PF charts diverge 118 vs 236 bars)—MIS can monitor rolling PF/recovery as regime-stability of the forecaster itself.
quote: The fact that the profit factor charts differ suggests that the model is unstable.

mechanism: Median of EMA(144) and EMA(169) defines Vegas tunnel center; Fibonacci offsets ±34/55/89/144/233/377 points form a dynamic lattice; map prior-bar Low/High into nearest lattice band to choose structural Stop levels—senses where price sits relative to medium-term tunnel geometry.
data_needed: EMA144, EMA169 closes; Point-scaled Fibo distances; High[1]/Low[1] vs lattice.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: FX charts with Vegas indicator; trailing demos on lower TFs noted as broker-sensitive
why_new_for_mis: Geometric structure sensor (price vs adaptive tunnel+Fibo bands) usable as regime/context feature for risk and trail logic, not only as an SL table.
quote: Applied Fibonacci levels are built according to Vegas Tunnel method here.

mechanism: Find last three consecutive same-side fractals; main trend line through fractals 1–2, lateral line through 2–3 after opposite-direction fractal post-breakout; require lateral line projection above/below main-line projection at fractal-1; lateral-line breakout flags sell in uptrend / buy in downtrend—senses trend end, flattening, or reversal.
data_needed: Fractal highs/lows (5-bar); line slopes V_down1/V_down2; PricePrL projections on current bar; optional MA144 slope and 25-bar range≥50 pts filter.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1; multi-day Oct sequence illustrated; Fork_Ch_ExpertH1
why_new_for_mis: Local fractal geometry sensor of trend exhaustion/flat onset via fork lateral break—MIS change flag complementary to MA crossovers.
quote: Lateral lines breaking through give rise to signals: to sell in the uptrend and to buy in the downtrend.

mechanism: Build fixed-height synthetic bars from tick stream: OPEN=first tick; update H/L until H−L exceeds ExtBarHeight then close (CLOSE equals H or L); no time binding—idle markets produce few bars, impulses many per minute—bar birth rate and equal-height OHLC become an activity/impulse clock for indicators.
data_needed: Tick stream or M1 history; ExtBarHeight in points (×10 on 5-digit); offline M9 chart feed.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD; M1 feed → synthetic M9 offline chart; compared vs daily time bars
why_new_for_mis: Price-move clock that converts volatility/activity into bar density—MIS can use synthetic-bar arrival rate as a real-time vol/impulse intensity sensor independent of wall-clock TF.
quote: there may be one synthetic bar in the chart (for hours) until the price starts moving, whereas a strong movement may result in a lot more than one bar over just a minute interval.

mechanism: Two upper + two lower fractals form converging channels if spacing/slope rules hold; compute pip/bar rates RatePriceH/S; project until lines meet (Apex) within 12–50 bars; actual breakthrough area = first ~2/3 of bars from base to Apex; invalidate pattern after zona time, delete drawings after Apex—senses timed breakout-validity window before apex crush.
data_needed: Four fractal prices/times; RatePriceH/RatePriceS; cut_left; T_period; time_starting/time_bar_zona/time_Apex.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: H1 Triangle_H1_v46 EA; tester report P/F≈2.36, ~101 deals
why_new_for_mis: Predictive time-to-apex and fractional breakthrough zone give MIS a finite-horizon change/breakout authenticity window rather than open-ended channel breaks.
quote: The distance between the vertical drawn through the second fractal and the middle vertical will form the actual breakthrough area.

mechanism: At h_beg (e.g. 20:00) set flat max=max(High[1],High[2]), min=min(Low[1],Low[2]); during Pacific/Asian night window trade only fades of boundary breaches with tight TP and wider SL; force-close and disable by h_end—explicit low-volatility night-flat regime sensor gated by clock.
data_needed: Server Hour(); two preceding bar H/L at session open; h_beg/h_end; optional deal-count caps.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURCHF, GBPCAD, EURCAD (also EURCHF session 18:00–10:00 cited); night flats
why_new_for_mis: Clock-bounded flat-regime detector with empirical boundary from pre-session bars—MIS session regime feature for low-vol mean-reversion vs day trend modes.
quote: The night flat usually lasts during the Pacific and Asian trading session and is characterized by low volatility of the majority of currency pairs.

mechanism: Observe that night spreads on EURCHF/GBPCAD/EURCAD widen 1.5–2× vs day; TP must shrink seasonally (e.g. EURCAD winter ~40 pts → ~20); treat spread inflation and seasonal flat quality as liquidity/tradability sensors that can invalidate the night-flat edge.
data_needed: Bid/Ask spread by hour and season; realized TP reach rates; intervention/news flags on legs (EURUSD, USDCHF for EURCHF).
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURCHF, GBPCAD, EURCAD night sessions; winter vs spring/summer reliability
why_new_for_mis: Session liquidity-cost sensor tied to the same flat regime—MIS can gate night strategies when spread/season metrics degrade, not only when vol rises.
quote: Night spreads are 1.5 to 2 times wider for the currencies that are especially good for night trading – EURCHF, GBPCAD and EURCAD.

mechanism: Include-file toolkit of order open/close/modify/trailing, MM modes, TimeLevel locks, and helper utilities—no market regime, vol, liquidity, or sequence sensing is constructed.
why_new_for_mis: After full read: developer scaffolding only; no MIS sensing idea.
quote: That is basically the entire list of the most needed Lite_EXPERT2.mqh functions which represent the sufficient minimum for convenient and efficient strategy tester writing in MQL4.

mechanism: Use ATR(period) on signal TF: (1) filter—require ATR to break its own average to confirm trend vs non-trend; (2) set SL/TP/trail distances as percent of ATR from bar Open with LevMinimum floor, recalculated each new bar—volatility-adaptive geometry replacing fixed-point stops.
data_needed: iATR; optional ATR signal average; Open[0]; STOPLOSS/TAKEPROFIT/TRAILINGSTOP as % of ATR; LevMinimum points.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EA examples on selectable TF (e.g. 240); JFatl direction + ATR sizing; news-breakout Exp_18 variant also ATR-scales stops
why_new_for_mis: Dual use of ATR as regime (trend/non-trend) filter and as a live volatility scale for levels—MIS vol-context feature that adapts to changing amplitude.
quote: Filtering signals of the trading system for identification of trend and non-trend market conditions. … the ATR indicator only provides an additional entry condition. Such additional condition can, for example, be the breakout of the average indicator value by the indicator itself.

mechanism: Detect sideways channel via support/resistance borders; fade borders while flat persists; abandon channel tactics on breakout (use stops)—strategy taxonomy that implicitly requires a flat-vs-trend regime switch versus trend-follow or against-trend modes.
data_needed: Support/resistance channel borders; price interaction with borders; Stop Loss beyond break.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Generic FX charts (illustrative); no single tested symbol/TF
why_new_for_mis: Explicit mapping of market state (sideways channel vs trending) to strategy class—MIS regime label that selects fade vs follow sensors.
quote: Such tactics are good for sideways trends (flats), but are not practically applicable in up-trends or down-trends.

mechanism: Compare Bollinger bands at short vs long averaging periods (e.g. 70 vs 370 min): longer-period bands are wider because short-period mean contributes to long-period dispersion; argue perceived 'trend' is often short-scale mean drift inside larger stationary dispersion—sensor of scale-dependent volatility vs trend illusion.
data_needed: Bollinger (or variance) at two+ averaging periods on same series; band width comparison.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: USDCHF M1 tester for related EA (tp=65,sl=41); Bollinger illustration periods 70 and 370 minutes
why_new_for_mis: Cross-scale dispersion sensor that questions trend labels—MIS can use short/long band-width ratio as a regime feature (local drift vs larger stationary envelope).
quote: Dispersion on a larger period is contributed by that what is mean value on a smaller period.

mechanism: Classify market as classical flat vs trend; longer flats (large-position formation / conversion masking) precede stronger subsequent trends; select historical pulse moves of target length (e.g. ≥130–140 pips one-pulse), mathematically describe start points via shared indicator parameters, then detect that pattern live—flat→impulse regime-change factory.
data_needed: Historical OHLC; labeled pulse segments of preset pip length; candidate indicator parameter sets; hit-rate vs statistical-error of pattern.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Conceptual FX/large-operator framing; no single backtest symbol locked
why_new_for_mis: Links measurable flat duration/structure to expected impulse strength and supplies a pattern-mining loop for regime-change start conditions—MIS sensing of transition readiness.
quote: The longer is the flat (the larger is the position and the period it is being formed), the stronger will be the following trend.
